status: version 13. Versions 1 to 4 were approved by the owner. Since 7 Oct 2026 a field is added by the rules when it passes the four tests, and the digest of the run that added it says so. The game reads this file.
about: Every field a thing may carry, and the only values that field may take. A field that does not apply to a thing is left out of that thing; it is never written as 'not applicable'. The wording is what a child sees or hears; it is not data.
rules: A field holds the everyday meaning, which is what the game sorts by.
An _academic field is added only where science disagrees with the everyday meaning. It never sorts a board and never marks a child wrong.

A new field enters this file in one of two ways, and the version number then goes up by one. Up to version 4 the owner approved each field and its values. Since 7 Oct 2026 the job adds a field when it passes four tests: every value has at least four familiar things; every thing it applies to has exactly one value, by two checks that agree; sample boards have one clean solution; and it is not an existing field in other words. Such a field says who added it.
A thing that truly fits more than one value of a field lists them all, and stays off boards sorted by that field.
The value 'depends' is only for things experts debate. It needs a note saying why, and such a thing also stays off boards sorted by that field.

An _academic field marked `only_where_science_differs` is carried only by the things for which a scientist's answer differs from the everyday one. It is absent everywhere else, and it never sorts a board.
A field marked `withdrawn` was taken back by the owner. It is kept, with the values things carry for it, and never sorts a board.

Since the owner's second ruling of 7 Oct 2026 a new field is a question from the field library (tools/content/field_library.json), which holds real ways of sorting from biology, geography and everyday life; such a field names its library question. A field may have more than four values, and a board uses any four of them that have enough familiar things.

kind_of_thing.wording: What kind of thing is it?

values.nature_not_alive: Things in nature that are not alive

animal: Think about something that is alive and can move on its own.
It can find its own food and eat it.
It can have babies, and it breathes and grows.
plant: Think about things that grow in the ground.
They are alive and they do not walk or fly.
They have roots, stems, and leaves, and they make their own food.
nature_not_alive: Think about things you can see outside that are not alive.
These things are not animals and not plants.
People do not make these things; they are just there in the world.
made_by_people: Think about things that are not found growing or walking on their own.
People use their hands and tools to make these things.
These things would not be here if nobody had made them.

in_between.label: Hard to place
clues: Think about things that do not fit in just one group.
They are a little like one kind of thing, and a little like another.
Even the people who study them do not agree where they belong.

kind_of_animal.wording: What kind of animal is it?

widened.tests: two checks put 6 of its things in it, none of the things already there, and found no place for its things among the kinds that were there

mammal: Think about animals that drink their mother's milk when they are babies.
These animals have hair or fur on their bodies.
These animals are warm when you touch them, even when it is cold outside.
bird: Think about animals that have feathers.
These animals have wings and a beak.
Most of them can fly, but some cannot.
fish: Think about a creature that lives in water all its life.
It breathes water through gills, not air.
It has fins to swim and no legs at all.
insect: Think about tiny creatures with six legs.
These little creatures often have wings too.
You can see many of them buzzing or crawling near you.
reptile: Think of animals whose skin is dry and covered in scales.
These animals are cold when you touch them, and they lie in the sun to get warm.
These animals have scaly skin and most of them lay eggs on land, not in water.
amphibian: Think about an animal that lives two lives.
It begins its life in water, as a little swimmer with a tail.
When it grows up it gets legs, and then it can live on land too.
dinosaur: Long, long ago, these animals lived on our Earth, and now we only see their bones.
Their bones are hard and old, and people dig them out of the ground to look at them.
These animals are not alive today at all — they all died out long before anyone's grandma was born.
arachnids: Think about a small creature with many legs.
Count its legs: there are eight, not six.
It has eight legs and no wings, and it is not an insect.

dinosaur_academic.wording: Is it a dinosaur to a scientist?

kind_of_dinosaur.wording: What kind of dinosaur is it?

land_hunter: Think about a dinosaur that eats other animals.
It hunts other dinosaurs on dry land, not in water or in the sky.
It has strong legs for running after its food, and sharp teeth for eating it.
land_grazer: Think about a dinosaur that eats green plants all day.
This dinosaur walks on the ground and eats plants, not meat.
This plant-eater stays on land and never flies or swims.
flyer: Think about a creature up in the sky with big wings.
This animal had wings and could fly, but it was not a bird.
Its wings were made of skin, and it flew high above the ground.
swimmer: Think about animals that live in the water all the time.
These animals swim in the sea and never walk on land.
They use flippers or paddles to move through the water.

extinct.wording: Is it extinct or still living?

kind_of_plant.wording: What kind of plant is it?

tree: Think about a plant with a big, hard stem called a trunk.
This plant grows very tall and has branches up high.
Birds like to sit and rest in this tall plant.
flower: Think of a plant part that is pretty to look at and smells nice.
This plant part is often put in a vase or given as a gift.
Bees and butterflies come to this bright, colourful part of a plant.
grass_grain: Think about plants with long, thin leaves.
These plants grow in big open fields, not in pots.
Many of these plants give us food we eat every day.
vegetable: Think about the plants we grow to eat at dinner.
We cook and eat these plants, not just look at them.
These plants go into our curry or our sabzi.

tree_academic.wording: Is it a tree to a scientist?

values.false: Not a tree to a scientist

kind_of_nature.wording: What kind of thing in nature is it?

sky: Think about what you see when you look up high above your head.
You can see these far away, but you cannot walk to them or touch them.
They look like they float or shine up above, not down here on the ground.
water: Think about something wet you can see outside.
It is not alive, but plants and animals need it.
It can be big or small, and it stays in one place or moves.
land: Think about a place you can walk on, outside.
It is a part of the ground, not water or sky.
You can stand on it and look around.
ground: Think about the hard ground under your feet.
You can pick it up, but it was never alive.
It is not water, not sky, and not a place you live.

kind_of_made_thing.wording: What do we use it for?

vehicle: Think about things that take people or loads from one place to another.
You do not carry it in your hand; you sit in it or climb on it to go somewhere.
It has wheels, or wings, or floats, and it moves you far away.
toy: Think about things you play with.
You hold them, move them, or make them go.
They are made just for fun, not for work.
household: Think about the things you find inside a home.
You use these every day, and they stay in one place.
These are not for going places or for playing; they help you live at home.
tool: Think about something you hold in your hand to help you do a job.
You use it to make or fix things, not to ride in or play with.
It is hard and strong, and it helps your hand do work like hitting, digging or cutting.
building: Think about places you can go inside or walk on.
People go to these places to do something or to get something.
Some are big and some are small, but people made them all.

part_we_eat.wording: Which part of the plant do we eat?
history: 24 Nov 2026: 'The seeds or pods' became 'The seeds'. The owner played the set and was caught by Ladies finger, a pod we eat whole like a fruit; with 'pods' in the name no clue could tell this group from the fruit. Its things (pea, bean, maize, cowpea) are the ones whose seeds we eat.

fruit: Think about the part of the plant that holds the seeds.
It grows where a flower was.
We eat this part, the one that has the plant's seeds inside it.
under_the_ground: Think about the part of a plant that hides down in the soil.
We dig it out of the ground to eat it.
It grows down low, under the dirt, not up high in the sun.
leaves: Think about the green, flat part of a plant that grows up in the sun.
We pick this green part and cook it, but we do not dig it up from under the soil.
We eat this soft green part, and we do not wait for a fruit or a seed to grow.
seeds_or_pods: Think about the little hard parts inside a plant that can grow into a new plant.
We take these out and cook them, not the soft juicy part around them.
We dry them and keep them in jars to eat later, like little hard bits.

crossed.why: the owner, 24 Nov 2026: circles cross; a question belongs to every thing it is true of

kind_of_plant_academic.wording: What kind of plant is it to a scientist?

road: Think about how people go from one place to another on land.
These things roll on wheels and stop for people or goods.
These things share the road with other traffic and need a driver or rider.
rails: Think about how a thing moves along a special path.
It rolls on two long metal lines.
It cannot turn away to the left or the right.
water: Think about where a thing can move along, not on a hard path.
It moves on something soft and wet that you can splash in.
It floats and moves on the water, not on land or in the sky.
air: Think about something that goes high above your head.
It does not need a road, a track, or water to move.
It stays up in the sky while it carries people or things.

kind_of_house_thing.wording: What kind of thing in the house is it?

values.eating: Things to eat and drink with

furniture: Think about the big, heavy things in a house that stay in one place.
You do not carry these around; they stay put and hold you or your things.
You sit on it, sleep on it, eat at it, or keep things inside it.
eating: Think about things we use when we are hungry or thirsty.
We hold these in our hands at the table when we eat.
We put food or drink on or in these, then it goes to our mouth.
cleaning: Think about things that help make a place clean.
You use them when something is dirty.
They help you wash or sweep away the dirt.
electric: Think about things in your house that need power to work.
These things stop working when the power goes off.
You must plug these things in or switch them on to use them.

what_happens_when_wet.wording: What happens when it gets wet?

withdrawn.why: it passed on groups padded with other names for mud; a name must now be a thing of its own

shape_of_the_land.wording: What is the land mostly like there?

values.hollow: Hollows and holes in the land

high: Think about land that goes up, up, up.
This land is tall and steep, not flat at all.
You would have to climb up to stand on this land.
flat: Think about land where you can see far, all around you.
The ground does not go up, and it does not go down.
It is wide and level, with no hill and no hole.
by_water: Think about a place where the ground meets the wet.
On one side there is land, and on the other there is water.
It is the edge of the land, right beside a sea, a river or a lake.
hollow: Think about a place where the ground goes down, not up.
It is a low or empty spot you could look down into.
It is a dip or a hole in the ground, not a flat or high place.

pet_farm_or_wild.wording: Is it mostly a pet, a farm animal or a wild animal?

crossed.why: the owner, 24 Nov 2026: circles cross; a question belongs to every thing it is true of

pet: Think about an animal that lives inside your house with you.
This animal likes to stay close to people and be cared for by them.
People feed it, keep it safe, and it stays with the family at home.
farm: Think about animals that live where a farmer can look after them.
These animals give the farmer food or wool or eggs to use.
The farmer keeps them in a yard, a coop or a field, not in the house.
wild_land: Think about an animal that nobody owns.
Nobody feeds it and nobody keeps it: it finds its own food.
It lives free, and it lives on land, not in water.
wild_water: Think about an animal that is at home where it is wet.
Nobody feeds it and nobody keeps it: it finds its own food.
It lives free, in the sea, in a river or a pond, or right beside one.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird.wording: Is it mostly a pet, a farm animal or a wild animal?

merged.why: it asks the same question as pet_farm_or_wild, which is now asked of the whole circle; its values are kept on the things

what_people_do_there.wording: What do people mostly do there?

live: Think about a place where a family stays.
People sleep there, cook there, and come back there every day.
learn: Think about a place full of books and questions.
Children and grown-ups go there to find things out.
A teacher helps people learn there.
pray: Think of a place where people go to talk to God.
People go there to sing, to pray, and to be quiet with God.
People sit together there and fold their hands to pray.
buy: Think about a place where money and things change hands.
People come here to get things they need or want, and they pay for them.
Here you can pick a thing up, pay money for it, and carry it home.
heal: Think about a place people go to when they are sick or hurt.
People go there to get well again.
travel: Think about a place where you go to begin a trip far away.
People wait there with bags, ready to go somewhere new.
You go there to get on a big thing that carries you away.
cross: Think about going from one side to the other side.
You do not stay here; you go across or go up.
It helps you get over something, like water or a road.

how_we_play_with_it.wording: How do we mostly play with it?

throw: Think about a toy that does not stay in your hands.
You send it away from you, and someone sends it back.
You throw it, kick it or hit it, and off it goes.
ride: Think about a toy that carries you.
You climb on it, and it holds you up.
You sit on it, and you ride, rock or roll along.
build: Think about making something new with your hands.
You put the pieces one on top of another.
When you finish, you have made a shape or a thing.
pretend: Think about a toy you hold close and love.
This toy is soft or small, and you use it in your arms or in make-believe.
You hug it, or you act like it is real in a story.
wheel: Think about a toy that rolls.
It has wheels, and your hand pushes or pulls it along the floor.
You do not sit on it: it rolls along on its own little wheels.
fly: Think about a toy that goes up in the air and floats.
You hold it with a string or your hand, and the air lifts it.
It moves through the air above you, not on the ground.
music: Think about toys that make sounds you can hear.
You use your hands or your mouth to make the sound come out.
The sound is music, not a bang or a beep.

dinosaur_group.wording: Which dinosaur family does it belong to?

withdrawn.why: its fourth group, bone-headed dinosaurs, has only two well-known members, so no set could open; the job may now propose five or six groups

what_it_eats.wording: What does this animal mostly eat?

eats_plants: Think about what grows green in the ground.
This animal's tummy is happy with grass and leaves.
It never wants meat or bugs, only green things.
eats_meat: This animal eats other animals, not plants.
It hunts other animals and eats only their meat.
Its food is meat, and it never eats plants or bugs.
eats_both: This animal eats two kinds of food, not just one.
It eats green things that grow, and also eats other animals.
Its tummy gets full from plants and from meat too.
eats_insects: Think about tiny crawling things with six legs.
These animals hunt for very small bugs to fill their tummies.
They use long noses or sticky tongues to catch little bugs.

how_it_makes_sound.wording: How does this toy make its sound?

hit_or_strike: Think about how your hand makes a sound on something.
You use a stick or your hand to tap it.
When you tap or bang it, it makes a loud sound.
blow_into: You use your breath to make the sound.
Your mouth goes on it, and the air goes in.
You blow in, and the air makes the music.
press_keys: Think about a toy you play with your fingers.
You do not hit it or blow it or pull its strings.
You touch small parts on top, and music comes out.
pluck_strings: Think about how your fingers touch the toy to start the sound.
You move your fingers along tight lines to make the sound.
Your fingers pull or sweep the tight lines, and they are not keys or holes.
